front: What is the acceleration of free fall near the Earth?
back: About 9.8 m/s² (g); some questions use 10 m/s².
Falling under gravity alone, with no air resistance.

front: Do heavy objects fall faster in a vacuum?
back: No: without air resistance all objects fall with the same acceleration g.
The constant maximum velocity reached when air resistance equals the weight of a falling object.

front: Why does a falling object's acceleration decrease?
back: Air resistance increases with speed, so the resultant force (weight − air resistance) decreases.

front: What is the resultant force at terminal velocity?
back: Zero: air resistance balances the weight.

front: What happens when a skydiver opens the parachute?
back: Air resistance becomes greater than the weight, so she decelerates to a lower terminal velocity.

front: Shape of the speed-time graph of a falling skydiver?
back: A curve starting with gradient ≈ 9.8 m/s² that levels off at terminal velocity.

front: How can g be measured in the laboratory?
back: Time a heavy ball falling a known height with light gates; use g = 2h/t².
